Under normal circumstances
Like steel
Strength and durability are the main indicators for evaluating the quality of concrete.
The cubic compressive strength of concrete is a very important strength value.
Because it is the basis for classifying concrete strength grades.
The standard specimen is a cube with a side length of 150 mm.
According to the "Code for Design of Concrete Structures"
It can be divided into 14 levels, from C15 to C80.
The axial tensile strength of concrete is a key factor in structural design.
Key indicators for determining the crack resistance of concrete
It can also be used to indirectly measure other mechanical properties of concrete.
For example, the punching shear strength of concrete.
Bond strength between concrete and steel reinforcement, etc.
The axial tensile strength test also uses a cube with a side length of 150 mm as the standard specimen.
What we need to pay attention to is
The axial tensile strength of concrete is much lower than its cubic strength.
It is only about 1/8 to 1/18 of the latter.
Moreover, this ratio decreases as the compressive strength grade of concrete increases.
In other words, the increase in tensile strength of concrete is slower than the increase in compressive strength.
The axial compressive strength of concrete is also known as the prism strength.
In actual engineering structures, most reinforced concrete compression members are prisms or cylinders.
In order to ensure that the measured compressive strength of concrete is close to the actual stress condition of the concrete structure.

Concrete deformation can be divided into two categories.
One type is deformation under load.
Such as the deformation of monotonic short-term loading
Deformation under long-term loading and deformation under repeated loading
Another type of deformation is unrelated to the force applied.
This is called volume deformation.
Such as the shrinkage of concrete and the expansion and deformation caused by temperature changes.
We consider the long-term action of the load
Stress remains constant but strain in concrete
The phenomenon of creep increasing over time is called concrete creep.
Additionally, during cement hydration and concrete hardening in air...
Both will reduce the volume of concrete.
This phenomenon is called contraction.
Because the shrinkage and creep of concrete can introduce additional internal forces into statically indeterminate structures.
It will also cause prestress loss in prestressed structures.
Close attention must be paid to the design calculations.

It is not a perfectly elastic body.
It is a type of elasto-plastic material.
When subjected to force, it produces recoverable elastic deformation.
It also produces irreversible plastic deformation.

The stress-strain relationship under short-term loading is not linear.
Instead, it is a curve as shown in the figure.
The stress-strain ratio varies with the stress in the concrete.
Therefore, the elastic modulus of concrete is much more complex than that of steel.
The elastic modulus of concrete is measured in standard specimens of concrete prisms.
The ratio of the specified compressive stress value obtained by standard test methods to its corresponding compressive strain value
According to relevant Chinese standards, the following method should be used to determine the elastic modulus Ec of concrete.
The experiment used prism specimens.
The upper limit of stress is taken as 0.5 times the axial compressive strength of concrete.
Then uninstall to zero.
Repeat the loading and unloading process up to 5 times.
10 times

The stress-strain curve is close to a straight line.

The slope of this straight line is used as the value of the elastic modulus of concrete.

We learned about the compressive modulus of elasticity of concrete.
How should its tensile modulus of elasticity be calculated?
Then we discovered
The ratio of the tensile modulus of elasticity to the compressive modulus of elasticity of concrete is 0.82 to 1.12.
The average is approximately 0.995, close to 1.
therefore
The standard approximates the tensile modulus of elasticity to be equal to the compressive modulus of elasticity.

Everyone knows how to calculate the tensile modulus of elasticity.
How then is the shear modulus of concrete determined?
According to elasticity theory
Relationship between shear modulus and elastic modulus
The shear modulus is equal to the sum of the elastic modulus divided by the Poisson's ratio of concrete + 1, and then multiplied by 2.
When Poisson's ratio is 0.2
The formula yields a shear modulus that is exactly 0.4 times the elastic modulus.
